# Porting an xscreensaver hack

The rules live in `AGENTS.md` ("Rules", "Gotchas") and the path-scoped notes in
`.claude/rules/`. This skill sets the order of work and the points to stop. The
numbered steps are in `adding-a-hack.md` and the recipes it names are in
`techniques.md`, both next to this file. For several hacks in one go, read
`batches.md` too.

## 1. Pick, then read the source

Take S-rated rows from `docs/porting-assessment.md` first, and prefer a low
**Speed** band: the table runs each unported S hack on the host. The effort
rating counts missing shim calls, not memory, speed or stack (Braid was S, and
would have shown as high). A high band is a hack that will probably run slowly
on the board; a low band is not a guarantee, because a hack still doing
software `double` maths runs far slower on the device than on the host. Read
the hack's source before copying it, and look for:

| The source has | Technique (seen in) |
| --- | --- |
| Arrays or a state over a few MB | Build-time patch (Maze) |
| `sin`, `cos`, `sqrt`, `pow`, `double` in a hot loop | Single precision (Galaxy, Substrate) |
| Locals over a few KB | Stack check (Rorschach) |
| An allocation of 100 KB or more, or `exit()` on failure | Large allocations (Substrate) |
| Pixmaps, clip masks, a logo image | Images (Maze) |
| A hack that restarts itself | Restart leak test (Maze, Substrate) |
| A `free` that relies on state `draw` sets up (a lazy `initted`) | Stopping before the first draw (Blaster) |
| Hairlines, fades or `glPolygonOffset` in a GL hack | Thin lines in a GL hack |
| Threads, GL, Xft, shared memory | Skipping a hack |
| A licence header | Read it; add a notices section only if it differs from jwz's |

## 2. Set up

Work in a worktree off `origin/main`. Its setup and the commands it refuses are
in "Worktree setup".

## 3. Red, copy, green

Follow `adding-a-hack.md`. Show the registry test failing before
copying. Fill each shim gap test-first, then break the code on purpose and
watch the test fail ("Tests that cannot be fooled"). Filling a missing
function is a shim gap. Changing what every hack sees (the runner, a default, a
shared helper) is not: stop and ask Rod first.

## 4. Verify on the host

Run `pio test -e native`, `uv run --with pytest --with pillow pytest tools/tests`
and `uv run tools/check_notices.py`, and dump frames at several counts. Host
frames cannot show a byte swap, which happens in the push to the display: judge
colour on the device, on a colour you know the answer to.

## 5. Device

Flash only after Rod says so in this conversation; approval for one flash is
not approval for the next. See "Device capture". Report "compiles", "host tests
pass" and "runs on the device" separately; only Rod can say what the screen
shows. If it is slow, measure, change one thing, flash again and compare; if it
is still slow, say so and suggest dropping it. Record the numbers in
`tools/assessment_measured.md`, marking anything unmeasured as such.

## 6. Deliver

Commit named paths. Open the draft PR with `entire trail create` and put what
is unverified in its body. After a rebase, a push needs `--force-with-lease`:
ask Rod each time. Rod approves and merges; then delete the branch and
fast-forward `main`. New gotchas go in the matching `.claude/rules/` file (or
`AGENTS.md` if they apply everywhere) in the same PR, and deferred
ideas become issues.

## Red flags

| Thought | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| "It is rated S, so I need not read it" | Maze was rated L for Xlib gaps; the real blocker was a 20 MB `calloc`. |
| "It compiles, so it works" | Rorschach compiled and rebooted on its first frame. |
| "The colours look right" | Not from a host frame: every hack was byte swapped until Maze. |
| "My test passes, so it tests something" | A test through Pyro passed with the runner broken. Break the code on purpose. |
| "AGENTS.md says to fix shim gaps, so I can change the runner" | A new function is a gap. A change every hack sees needs Rod. |
| "Rod approved flashing earlier" | Ask again for each flash. |

# Porting a batch of hacks

For several hacks on one branch, with Rod away. The per-hack steps are in
`SKILL.md` and `adding-a-hack.md`; this is what a batch adds. Per-hack findings
live in `.claude/rules/hacks.md`, not here.

## Order of work

1. Read every header before copying anything: a `(GPL)` tag or an xlock notice
   changes the notices row, and a licence that is not a permission notice means
   stop and ask.
2. Triage by gap count. Do the easy ones first: they pay for shim gaps the
   others need. Leave GL and anything under a few fps to last.
3. One branch, a commit per hack, shim code test-first and mutation-checked.
   No PR until Rod says.
4. `uv run tools/wire_hack.py <name> <Class> "<copyright>"` copies the file and
   registers it with a frame hash of `0` (skipped), so every commit stays green.
   Then `pio run -e dump`, fill the gaps, dump frames at several counts and
   look at them.
5. Flash and measure each hack as soon as it runs
   (`bash tools/flash_and_capture.sh <hack> 30`). Report measured, unjudged and
   unseen separately.
6. Pin all the new hashes in one run, after looking at the frames:
   `HACK_PINS_OUT=<file> pio test -e native -f test_hacks`.
7. Measured rows, rules, a regenerated assessment, and a notes file for Rod: what
   to look at, which choices are his, what was not measured.

## Traps

| Trap | Do |
| --- | --- |
| A change that is not pixel-identical by construction (single precision, a faster fill) and you only checked fps | Look at a frame. A hack drew garbage for hours at "20 fps" |
| `#define double float` before a header that has `double` in a struct a shim `.c` shares | Include that header first, then the define; a flat-screen test guards it |
| A hack that keeps state in statics across starts | Its pin depends on earlier tests; reset the static in a wrapper, and test both outcomes |
| A mode picked with `random()` | A boot is deterministic, so measure the other mode by forcing it |
| Constants in pixels or frames, tuned for another window size or frame rate | Scale them at build time (`tools/fireworkx_patch.py`), not by editing the copy |
| A hack that treats `malloc(0) == NULL` as out of memory | The board returns NULL for zero bytes, the host a pointer: it stops drawing on the board only. Reproduce with an allocator hook that fails for zero |
| A stop that leaks | `MallocStackLogging=1 leaks --atExit -- .pio/build/dump/program <index> 0 out.raw` names the line (rebuild `-e dump` first) |

## Finding the cost

Skip one thing behind a temporary flag and read `step=`; revert it. Guessing
was wrong three times running. The usual causes here:

- full-frame passes over PSRAM: a clear, a copy, a blur, a 565 conversion (render
  smaller, alias a pixmap to the window, erase only what was drawn)
- the shim's polygon fill, which divides in double (`hacks/float_polygon.h`)
- soft double: `xtensa-esp32s3-elf-nm <object> | grep ' U __.*df'`; `frand` hides
  a `1.0` in its macro body (`hacks/single_frand.h`)
- a pause the hack asks for (`wait=`): override `*delay` and say the pace changed

## Choices for Rod

When look and speed trade off, leave a build flag per option, measure each, and
register the one nearer his bar. After his hands-on notes, expect to retune.

## Tools

| Need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Register a hack | `tools/wire_hack.py` |
| Flash a pinned build and read the serial log | `tools/flash_and_capture.sh`, `tools/serial_capture.py` |
| Does a test notice a break | `tools/mutate.py <file> 'old=>new' --cmd '...'` |
| Pin hashes | `HACK_PINS_OUT` (above) |
# Adding a hack

Moved verbatim from AGENTS.md. The order of work is in `SKILL.md`.

The `port-hack` skill orders this work, says what to read for before copying a
hack, and holds a recipe per trap. The steps:

1. Check its row in `docs/porting-assessment.md` (effort and Speed band) and
   read its licence header.
2. Update the expected list in `firmware/test/test_hacks/test_hacks.c` and see
   it fail.
3. Copy the file to `firmware/src/hacks/<name>/<name>.c`, add the notices row
   and an `extern` plus entry in `hacks/registry.c`.
4. Fill shim gaps test-first in `firmware/test/test_xshim/`. The compile
   check in `score_hacks.py` shows what is missing.
5. Host tests pass, dump a frame and look at it, then (with Rod's go-ahead)
   flash and measure fps and free heap/PSRAM over serial. To pin its frame
   hash after looking at the frame, put `0x1ull` in `kBaseline`, run
   `pio test -e native -f test_hacks`, convert the "Was N" in the failure line
   with `python3 -c "print(hex(N))"`, and run it again.
6. Regenerate the assessment and add measurements to
   `tools/assessment_measured.md`, then re-run the speed backtest: each port
   adds a point to the check of the Speed bands, which were fitted to the first
   29 hacks. To make a port a real test, commit its host time and predicted
   range first (`docs/speed-predictions.md` shows the form), flash it as copied,
   and add its name to `HOLDOUT` in `tools/speed_backtest.py`. The first four
   (Mountain, Epicycle, Kaleidescope, Celtic) all fell where predicted.
7. If a hack is slow and `double`-heavy (many `double`s, `sqrt`, `sin`/`cos`,
   `pow`), try a single-precision wrapper like `hacks/galaxy_single.c` (for a
   plain screenhack, `hacks/substrate_single.c`; the recipe is in the skill's
   `techniques.md`), and compare double and float frames at several frame
   counts. A resource
   override can skip a hack's restart cleanup: Galaxy leaked at `count: 2`, so
   leak-test any override.
8. If Rod drops a port after seeing it (Celtic): remove it from `g_hacks[]`, the
   expected list, its hash and its leak test; keep the source and notices row;
   add `name: reason` (short: it is printed as a bullet) to
   `tools/failed_ports.txt`; file an issue.

# Per-hack gotchas

Moved verbatim from the Gotchas section of AGENTS.md.

- Maze keeps a 1000 by 1000 maze and three 1,000,000-entry move lists in one
  `calloc` (about 20 MB; the board has 8 MB of PSRAM). `hacks/maze/maze.c`
  stays byte-identical: `firmware/patch_maze.py` (a PlatformIO `pre:` script
  in every env) writes a copy with both limits at 80 into the build dir, using
  `tools/maze_patch.py`, which fails loudly if upstream's `#define`s change.
  `hacks/maze_small.c` includes that copy and the original is excluded from
  `build_src_filter`. A `gridSize` below 7 would overflow the 80 by 80 arrays.
- Pacman has two build-time patches (`tools/pacman_patch.py`, run by
  `firmware/patch_pacman.py`; wrappers `hacks/pacman_stdlevel.c` and
  `hacks/pacman_loop_ai.c`): it always plays the fixed level, because the
  random generator recursed to ~315 KB and boot-looped the board, and the
  ghosts' route search is a loop (it was 453 levels deep). Each patch checks
  what it replaces. Its sprite sheet is built from `vendor/` into the build dir
  by `firmware/pacman_sprites.py` and never committed (3 MB as C text).
- Braid runs at 3-9 fps (0.8-2 before four rounds of work): it redraws every
  segment of the braid each frame to spin the colours. A host profile put its
  disc fill at 6% and the board spent most of its time there, because the Mac
  does `double` at full speed. Split a slow hack's step on the device with a
  temporary flag that returns early from the expensive call.
- Maze fills the whole 466 by 466 square, so its corners and the exit marker
  fall outside the round display's visible circle.
- `check_notices.py` reads 100 lines of header: Maze's licence follows a long
  modification history.
- A hack can be freed before its first draw: two quick presses, or a press
  with the 90 s rotation. `test_every_hack_can_be_stopped_before_its_first_frame`
  runs every hack through it. Blaster's free dereferenced NULL (it sizes a loop
  in init but allocates in draw), so `hacks/blaster_safe.c` includes the
  unmodified hack with `XSCREENSAVER_MODULE` emptied and registers it with a
  free that zeroes `NUM_ROBOTS` when `robots` is NULL.
- Deluxe is built through `hacks/deluxe_opaque.c`, which includes the unmodified
  hack with `XSCREENSAVER_MODULE` emptied and registers it with overrides:
  `*transparent: False` (upstream's plane masks need colour planes, which
  `allocate_alpha_colors` reports none of) and `*doubleBuffer: False` (it was
  added when the shim drew only on the canvas, so the `XCopyArea` from its
  blank pixmap erased the picture; pixmaps work now, but two 434 KB back
  buffers and a full-frame copy each frame would cost more than they give).
  The wrapper then gives each throbber's GC an alpha of 26
  of 32 (upstream's translucent weight) and sends full wide circles to
  `stroke_circle`. A plain screenhack's `HackEntry` has no overrides unless a
  wrapper builds it. Its step is 45-63 ms on the device against a 32.5 ms push,
  so about 11-13 fps; ideas for more are in issue #54.
- Eight of the S-hack batch (Anemone, Anemotaxis, Compass, FuzzyFlakes,
  Halftone, Interaggregate, LMorph, Wormhole) are built through
  `hacks/<name>_direct.c` (pixmap double buffering, see `techniques.md`;
  LMorph's is `lmorph_single.c` because it needs no `HAVE_JWXYZ`). All but
  Anemotaxis and Wormhole, and Euler2D (`euler2d_single.c`), also use
  `single_precision.h` plus build-time float literals (`patch_float_literals.py`
  lists them). `single_precision.h` leaves `floor` and `ceil` on the double
  versions: Euler2D's wrapper maps them itself. After the literal pass, `nm`
  still shows soft-double helpers in Euler2D, Halftone, Interaggregate and
  Anemone; their source was not chased.
- `test_frames_of_every_hack_but_maze_match_main` stops at the first hash that
  differs, in registry order, so repinning several hacks takes one test run
  each (about 85 s), earliest first. A hack whose frames do not change under a
  wrapper (Compass and Halftone in single precision) keeps its hash.
- Anemone's step moves between 31 and 56 ms as its arms grow and shrink, so its
  fps is 11 to 15.5 whatever one 20 s window says. Forest waits 500 ms between
  trees by design (about 2 fps, and the push is 88 rows).
- A hack that unpacks pixel values itself (Substrate and Interaggregate, in
  their `point2rgb`) assumes ordinary RGB565, but the canvas holds the bytes
  swapped. Its wrapper swaps pixels where they cross `XAllocColor` and
  `XSetForeground`. Interaggregate shipped without this: its alpha blends
  mixed the wrong bit fields and drew rainbow noise instead of green and brown
  strokes. `test_interaggregate_blend` includes the wrapper to check one blend.
- `dump` never seeds `random()`, so a hack that picks a mode at start (Truchet,
  12 modes) shows the same one in every dump. To see others, build the hack
  alone (`probe_hacks.registry_source` and `shim_sources`) from a copy outside
  `vendor/`, with a `__attribute__((constructor))` that calls
  `srandom(atoi(getenv("SEED")))`. A device boot is deterministic too (Halo
  chose Ramp on five boots in a row), so a hack that picks a mode with
  `random()` always starts the same one: force another with a temporary
  `*mode:` override to measure it. Rotation reaches other modes because the
  random state differs by then.
- Hexadrop (`hexadrop_single.c`) runs at about 10 fps, under the 15 fps bar.
  Splitting its step on the device showed the maths and the edge walk cost
  0.1 ms and all the rest is canvas writes: about 860 KB of 16-bit stores
  into the PSRAM canvas a frame. Single precision, a float convex fill and
  two-pixel stores took it from 2.4 to 10.2 fps with pixel-identical frames.
  More needs a shared canvas change or rasterising in row bands.
- Halo (`halo_direct.c`, `halo_planes.h`, `halo_circles.h`) draws whole circles
  into 1-bit pixmaps and XORs two of them. Its pixmaps are packed bit planes
  (27 KB each), not colour pixmaps: 434 KB colour stand-ins made Seuss mode
  (three runs in four) 5-9 fps, because window-sized circles are millions of
  PSRAM writes, and a float circle fill alone changed nothing. A device boot
  is deterministic, so every boot picked Ramp mode and hid that: force
  `*colorMode: seuss` temporarily to measure the other mode. It overrides
  `*delay` to 10 ms (upstream asks for 100 ms), so the circles grow faster.
- StonerView's seven files are built as one unit by `stonerview_gl.c`.
  Upstream never frees its oscillator list ("how do we free this?"), so the
  wrapper frees it through the `next` links before upstream's release.
- XMatrix needs `matrix_glyphs.py` (a `pre:` script in every env), which
  converts four PNGs from `vendor/` into blobs in the build directory: they
  are never committed (1.5 MB of C text each for the large sheets). It
  registers through `xmatrix_direct.c` with `*trace: False`, which skips the
  typed "connecting" sequence it would open with (the rare "Knock, knock,
  Neo" event, `knockKnock`, is still on); `*matrixFont: small`
  gives 46 columns instead of 23. Its text modes read no text: the
  `textclient.h` stand-in never opens a source, and Xt timers never fire.
- Flurry is not ported. It draws 3,600 blended, textured quads a frame and
  needs `glAlphaFunc`, `glRectd`, `gluBuild2DMipmaps` and luminance-alpha
  textures, none in TinyGL here. With `gl_budget.py`'s per-vertex and
  per-pixel costs that is well under 1 fps (arithmetic, not a measurement:
  the tool cannot read a multi-file hack).
- Qix and Fireworkx both leaked on every stop, found by the restart leak test.
  Qix's `qix_free` skips each segment's `lines[i].p` array (about 48 KB per
  stop); Fireworkx below 24 bits never frees its own 565 image buffer (48 KB).
  Their wrappers (`qix_direct.c`, `fireworkx_single.c`) free the missing piece
  before calling upstream's free. LeakSanitizer does not run on macOS, but
  `MallocStackLogging=1 leaks --atExit -- .pio/build/dump/program <index> 0
  out.raw` names the allocating line in seconds (rebuild `-e dump` first: a
  `pio test` deletes the program).
- Starfish and Goop spent most of a frame in the shim's polygon fill (double
  maths per edge per row). `hacks/float_polygon.h` fills any even-odd polygon
  in float, optionally mixed in at an alpha in 32nds (all three colour
  channels with one multiply), and took Starfish from 8.5 to 19 fps. Goop draws
  straight onto the window (its `XCreatePixmap` is the window and the
  `XCopyArea` is skipped) and blends each blob in at the alpha upstream's jwxyz
  path uses. Its full-frame clear cost 15 ms, so `hacks/span_erase.h` erases
  only the bounding boxes the blobs filled last frame (pixel-identical frames):
  14.6-15.2 fps translucent. The shared `canvas_fill_polygon` is still double
  (Hexadrop has its own convex float fill). Goop is built through
  `goop_direct.c` with `HAVE_JWXYZ`; the colour-plane path needs planes the
  canvas lacks.
- A wrapper that does `#define double float` must include any header with a
  `double` in a struct the shim's `.c` files also use BEFORE the define: the
  hack includes it again, the guard keeps the copy seen through the macro, and
  the two sides disagree on the layout. `spline.h` did this to Starfish and
  Goop: they drew garbage (flat colours) at 16-20 fps and their first pinned
  hashes were of it. Look at a frame after any change that is not
  pixel-identical by construction;
  `test_hacks_that_use_the_spline_draw_a_real_picture` now fails on a flat
  screen.
- Fireworkx renders at 1/`FIREWORKX_SCALE` of the width and height
  (`hacks/lowrez_put.h`: it is told the window is smaller and `XPutImage`
  draws each pixel as a square): 2.4 fps as copied, 11 at a scale of 3, 12.4 at
  4. Its glow, flash pass and 565 conversion are full-frame walks over PSRAM.
  Its header says "(GPL)" but the text is the standard permission notice.

"""Check that every copied third-party source has a licence notice and is
listed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

Run with: uv run tools/check_notices.py
"""

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# Copied third-party code: one directory per hack under hacks/ (top-level
# files in hacks/ are our own, e.g. the registry), plus xs_support/.
SUFFIXES = {".c", ".h", ".cpp"}
HEADER_LINES = 100
NOTICE_PHRASES = (
    "permission to use, copy, modify, distribute, and sell this software",
    "permission is hereby granted, free of charge",
    "permission to use, copy, modify, and distribute this software",
)


def has_notice(text: str) -> bool:
    lines = (line.lstrip(" \t/*") for line in text.splitlines()[:HEADER_LINES])
    head = " ".join(" ".join(lines).split()).lower()
    return "copyright" in head and any(p in head for p in NOTICE_PHRASES)


def check(src_dir: Path, notices_md: Path) -> list[str]:
    notices = notices_md.read_text() if notices_md.exists() else ""
    problems = []
    candidates = sorted((src_dir / "hacks").glob("*/**/*")) + sorted(
        (src_dir / "xs_support").rglob("*")
    )
    for path in candidates:
        if path.suffix not in SUFFIXES or not path.is_file():
            continue
        rel = path.relative_to(src_dir)
        if not has_notice(path.read_text(errors="replace")):
            problems.append(f"{rel}: no licence notice in first {HEADER_LINES} lines")
        if path.name not in notices and path.stem not in notices:
            problems.append(f"{rel}: not listed in {notices_md.name}")
    # TinyGL's sources carry no per-file header, so it is checked as a
    # directory: its LICENSE beside the sources, and a mention in the notices.
    tinygl = src_dir / "tinygl"
    if tinygl.is_dir():
        if not (tinygl / "LICENSE").is_file():
            problems.append("tinygl: no LICENSE file")
        if "TinyGL" not in notices:
            problems.append(f"tinygl: not mentioned in {notices_md.name}")
    return problems


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--src", default=str(root / "firmware" / "src"))
    parser.add_argument("--notices", default=str(root / "THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md"))
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    problems = check(Path(args.src), Path(args.notices))
    for problem in problems:
        print(problem)
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

# GitHub Flavored Markdown Generation

**Version:** 1.2.1

Generate GFM that passes markdownlint validation with zero violations.

## Core Principles

### 1. Blank Lines Are Mandatory

- Before/after ALL lists (MD032)
- Before/after ALL headings except document start (MD022)
- Before/after ALL code blocks (MD031)
- Between ALL block-level elements

### 2. Consistency Required

- Use `-` for lists
- Use `#` for headings (ATX)
- Regular spaces only—never tabs/nbsp

### 3. Structure Matters

- Heading hierarchy: 1→2→3 (not 1→3)
- ONE H1 per document
- Files end with one newline
- Lines under 80 chars

### 4. Invisible Characters Matter

- Use ONLY regular spaces (U+0020)
- Never non-breaking spaces (U+00A0,  )
- Never tabs
- UTF-8 encoding

## Pre-Generation Checklist

- [ ] Where will lists/headings/code appear?
- [ ] Heading levels verified (1→2→3)?
- [ ] Using `-` for all lists?
- [ ] Code languages specified?
- [ ] Lines under 80 chars?
- [ ] Line breaks needed? (two trailing spaces)
- [ ] Using regular spaces only?
- [ ] URLs wrapped in `<>` or `[]`?
- [ ] Document starts with H1?
- [ ] Ordered lists use `1.` for all items?
- [ ] File ends with single newline?
- [ ] Tables use consistent spacing?

## Essential Rules

### Lists (MD032, MD004)

```markdown
Text before.

- Item one
- Item two

Text after.
```

### Headings (MD001, MD022)

```markdown
Text.

## Heading

Content.
```

### Code Blocks (MD031, MD040)

````markdown
Text.

```python
code()
```

Text.
````

**Nested Fences:** When showing markdown examples that contain code blocks,
use **one more backtick** than the deepest level:

- Three backticks (` ``` `): Regular code
- Four backticks (` ```` `): Markdown examples with code
- Five backticks (` ````` `): Nested markdown examples

`````markdown
````markdown
# Example

```bash
command
```

````
`````

### Line Length (MD013)

Break long lines at natural points. Use reference-style links for long URLs.

### URLs and Email (MD034)

Wrap bare URLs and emails:

```markdown
Wrong: https://example.com
Right: <https://example.com>
Right: [link](https://example.com)

Wrong: user@example.com
Right: <user@example.com>
```

### Document Structure (MD041)

Start with H1 (or front matter then H1):

```markdown
# Document Title

First paragraph.
```

### Ordered Lists (MD029)

Use `1.` for all items:

```markdown
1. First
1. Second
1. Third
```

### File Endings (MD047)

End with single newline:

```text
Last content line.
[single newline]
[EOF]
```

### Table Column Style (MD060)

Use consistent spacing in tables. Three styles:

**Compact (recommended):** `| cell |` - single space around content

```markdown
| Header 1 | Header 2 |
| --- | --- |
| Data | More data |
```

**Aligned:** Pipes vertically aligned with padding

**Tight:** `|cell|` - no spaces

Pick ONE style per document. Compact is preferred.

### Character Encoding

**Detection:** View → Render Whitespace in VS Code

**Fix:** Find `\u00A0` → Replace with space

**Critical for AI:** Two trailing spaces = intentional line breaks. Do NOT
remove them.

## Critical Error Patterns

### 1. List Without Blank Lines

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD032 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
Text:
- Item
Text.
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD032 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
Text:

- Item

Text.
```

### 2. Heading Without Blank Lines

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD022 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
Text.
## Head
Text.
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD022 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
Text.

## Head

Text.
```

### 3. Code Without Blanks/Language

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD031 MD040 -->

**Wrong:**

````markdown
Text:
```
code
```
Text.
````

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD031 MD040 -->

**Right:**

````markdown
Text:

```python

```

Text.
````

### 4. Inconsistent Markers

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD004 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
- Item
* Item
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD004 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
- Item
- Item
```

### 5. Skipping Levels

<!-- markdownlint-disable MD001 -->

**Wrong:**

```markdown
# Title

### Sub (skipped H2)
```

<!-- markdownlint-enable MD001 -->

**Right:**

```markdown
# Title

## Section

### Sub
```

## Post-Generation Validation

1. Lists have blank lines before/after
2. Headings have blank lines before/after
3. Code has blank lines before/after
4. Heading progression: 1→2→3→4
5. All lists use `-`
6. All code has language
7. Lines under 80 chars
8. Document starts with H1
9. URLs wrapped properly
10. Ordered lists use `1.`
11. File ends with one newline
12. Two trailing spaces used intentionally
13. Only regular spaces (no nbsp/tabs)
14. Tables use consistent column spacing

Markdown is **blocks with mandatory spacing:**

```text
[Text Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[Heading Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[List Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓
[Code Block]
↓ BLANK LINE ↓

**Programming:** `python` `javascript` `java` `c` `cpp` `go` `rust` `ruby`
`php` `swift` `kotlin` `typescript`

**Shell:** `bash` `sh` `powershell` `cmd` `zsh`

**Database:** `sql` `postgresql` `mysql`

**Other:** `text` `diff` `log`

```

Goal: Zero errors/warnings.

See bundled references:

- `references/complete-rules.md` - Full rule catalog
- `references/edge-cases.md` - Platform quirks
- `references/examples.md` - Detailed examples

Most common: Missing blank lines around lists/headings/code.

**Two trailing spaces:** Intentional line breaks. Do NOT remove.

#!/bin/bash
# Flashes a build that starts on one hack with rotation off, then reads the
# serial log. Needs the board, and Rod's say-so in the session (AGENTS.md:
# never flash without asking, unless he has said it is allowed).
#
#   bash tools/flash_and_capture.sh <hack> <seconds> [extra build flags] [lines]
#
# <hack> is a name from g_hacks[] in any case; extra flags are things like
# "-DFIREWORKX_SCALE=2"; the last `run` lines (default 6) are printed. The full
# log and the flash output go to $OUT_DIR (default: ./flash-capture, which
# should be somewhere git ignores, such as your scratchpad).
set -u
[ $# -ge 2 ] || { sed -n '2,12p' "$0"; exit 2; }
hack=$1 seconds=$2 extra=${3:-} lines=${4:-6}
repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
out=${OUT_DIR:-./flash-capture}
mkdir -p "$out"
out=$(cd "$out" && pwd)

source "$repo/tools/env.sh"
cd "$repo/firmware" || exit 1
PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS="-DSTART_HACK=\\\"$hack\\\" -DROTATE_SECONDS=0 $extra" \
  NO_COLOR=1 pio run -e stopwatch -t upload > "$out/flash_$hack.txt" 2>&1
pio_status=$?
unset PLATFORMIO_BUILD_FLAGS
verified=$(grep -c 'Hash of data verified' "$out/flash_$hack.txt")
echo "flash verified: $verified" "$(grep -E 'Flash:' "$out/flash_$hack.txt")"
grep -E "error:|overflowed" "$out/flash_$hack.txt" | head -3
# A failed flash leaves the old firmware running, and the capture would measure
# that: stop rather than report numbers for the wrong build.
if [ "$pio_status" -ne 0 ] || [ "$verified" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "flash failed (pio exit $pio_status, $verified verified); see $out/flash_$hack.txt" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "note: the board now starts on $hack with rotation off; flash a normal build when done"
"$repo/.venv/bin/python" -I "$repo/tools/serial_capture.py" "$out/$hack.log" "$seconds"
grep -a "^run" "$out/$hack.log" | tail -"$lines" | cut -c1-125

 * single-precision only, so `double` maths runs in software) and
 * with its decimal literals made floats at build time

 * system double-buffers for the hack, and the hack then draws straight on the
 * window. The shim can draw into pixmaps, but a back buffer would cost 434 KB
 * and a full-frame copy each frame, and would dirty every row. */
#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "screenhack.h"

#include "hacks/single_precision.h"

#undef XSCREENSAVER_MODULE
#define XSCREENSAVER_MODULE(CLASS, PREFIX)

/* Included by the *_single.c wrappers just before the unmodified hack source,
 * after every header the hack needs, so shared structs keep their `double`
 * layout. The ESP32-S3's FPU is single-precision only: `double` and the double
 * libm calls run in software. */
#ifndef HACKS_SINGLE_PRECISION_H
#define HACKS_SINGLE_PRECISION_H

#define double float
#define sqrt(x) sqrtf(x)
#define sin(x) sinf(x)
#define cos(x) cosf(x)
#define atan(x) atanf(x)
#define atan2(y, x) atan2f(y, x)
#define exp(x) expf(x)
#define fabs(x) fabsf(x)
#define fmod(x, y) fmodf(x, y)
#define pow(x, y) powf(x, y)
#define log(x) logf(x)

_Static_assert(sizeof(double) == sizeof(float),
               "single_precision.h must be in effect");

#endif
